newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel eases rules on foreign currency.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel eases rules on foreign currency.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Monday it would allow Israelis to invest more freely in overseas securities markets as part of a package of foreign-currency liberalisation measures.
The central bank also said it had sent to the Treasury a wider range of foreign currency-liberalisation proposals for its approval.

Under the announced measures, Israelis will be permitted to invest in all foreign publicly traded securities so long as the shares are quoted on a widely available network. Israelis will also be permitted to participate in initial public offerings that meet the same criteria.

Until now, Israelis were limited to investing in securities traded on officially approved exchanges. That prohibited them from investing in certain Eurobonds and foreign mutual funds, the Bank of Israel noted.

In addition, the bank said Israelis would be able to place funds obtained from a foreign currency loan, whether from a domestic or overseas bank, in a designated foreign currency account. The new rules will also apply to the proceeds from the sale of a foreign security, even if the security was originally purchased in Israeli shekels.
Up until now the Bank of Israel had required citizens to convert foreign currency funds into shekels within 30 days of receipt.

The bank also said it would allow travellers going abroad to buy foreign currency without presenting an airline ticket or other documents. The $7,000 ceiling on currency purchases, however, remains in effect, the bank said.
The bank also eased rules on taking assets out of the country and providing financial assistance to Israelis studying abroad.
